content: The text provided is a long and detailed transcription of references and systematic reviews related to physical activity, health outcomes, and interventions in various populations, including older adults, pregnant women, and community-dwelling individuals. 1. Elen JGZ conducted a systematic review examining the relationship between social support and physical activity in older adults. The findings were published in the International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity in 2017, volume 14, issue 1, article 56. 2. McMullan II, McDonough SM, Tully MA, Cupples M, Casson K, and Bunting BP performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate the association between balance and free-living physical activity in older adults residing in the community. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2018, volume 18, article 431. 3. Sherrington C, Fairhall NJ, Wallbank GK, Tiedemann A, Michaleff ZA, Howard K, et al. reviewed the role of exercise in preventing falls among older adults living in the community. Their findings were published in The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019, issue 1, article CD012424. 4. Sivaraman D, Fitzsimons C, Kelly P, Ludwig K, Mutrie N, Saunders DH, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to compare the effects of yoga with active and inactive controls on physical function and health-related quality of life in older adults. The results were published in the International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity in 2019, volume 16, article 33. 5. Taylor LM, Kerse N, Frakking T, and Maddison R performed a meta-analysis to evaluate the impact of active video games on physical performance measures in older adults. This study was published in Journal of Geriatric Physical Therapy in 2018, volume 41, issue 2, pages 108–123. 6. Vancampfort D, Lara E, Smith L, Rosenbaum S, Firth J, Stubbs B, et al. explored the relationship between physical activity and loneliness in adults aged 50 years or older across six lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in International Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry in 2019, volume 34, issue 12, pages 1855–1864. 7. Yoshimura Y, Wakabayashi H, Yamada M, Kim H, Harada A, and Arai H conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to assess interventions for treating sarcopenia. The results were published in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association. 8. Shea BJ, Reeves BC, Wells G, Thuku M, Hamel C, Moran J, et al. developed AMSTAR 2, a critical appraisal tool for systematic reviews that include randomized or non-randomized studies of healthcare interventions. This tool was described in BMJ in 2017, volume 358, article j4008. 9. Gillespie LD, Robertson MC, Gillespie WJ, Sherrington C, Gates S, Clemson LM, et al. reviewed interventions aimed at preventing falls in older adults living in the community. Their findings were published in The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012, issue 9, article CD007146. 10. Lefebvre C, Manheimer E, and Glanville J authored Chapter 6 of the Cochrane Handbook, which focuses on searching for studies. This chapter is part of the Cochrane Collaboration's guidelines, updated in March 2011. 11. Sherrington C, Fairhall N, Wallbank G, Tiedemann A, Michaleff ZA, Howard K, et al. provided an abridged Cochrane systematic review on exercise for preventing falls in older adults living in the community. This was published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2019. 12. Lamb SE, Becker C, Gillespie LD, Smith JL, Finnegan S, Potter R, et al. developed a taxonomy to classify and describe fall-prevention interventions in clinical trials. This work was published in Trials in 2011, volume 12, article 125. 13. Higgins JPT, Green S, and the Cochrane Collaboration published the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions in 2011, providing comprehensive guidance for conducting systematic reviews. 14. Schünemann HJ, Higgins JP, Vist GE, Glasziou P, Akl EA, et al., on behalf of the Cochrane GRADEing Methods Group, authored Chapter 11 of the Cochrane Handbook, which focuses on completing Summary of Findings tables and grading the quality of evidence. 15. Norway C provided guidance on writing plain language summaries for Cochrane intervention reviews, accessible as of November 15, 2017. 16. Serra-Prat M, Sist X, Domenich R, Jurado L, Saiz A, Roces A, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of an intervention to prevent frailty in pre-frail older adults consulting in primary care. This randomized controlled trial was published in Age and Ageing in 2017, volume 46, issue 3, pages 401–407. 17. Yu R, Wong M, Leung J, Lee J, Auyeung TW, and Woo J investigated the incidence, reversibility, risk factors, and protective effects of high body mass index against sarcopenia in community-dwelling older Chinese adults. Their findings were published in Geriatrics & Gerontology International in 2014, volume 14, supplement 1, pages 15–28. 18. Henwood TR, Riek S, and Taaffe DR compared strength-specific and muscle power-specific resistance training in community-dwelling older adults. This study was published in Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2008, volume 63, issue 1, pages 83–91. 19. Lustosa LP, Silva JP, Coelho FM, Pereira DS, Parentoni AN, and Pereira LS assessed the impact of a resistance exercise program on functional capacity and knee extensor strength in pre-frail older women. This randomized crossover trial was published in Revista Brasileira de Fisioterapia in 2011, volume 15, issue 4, pages 318–324. 20. Oh SL, Kim HJ, Woo S, Cho BL, Song M, Park YH, et al. evaluated the effects of an integrated health education and elastic band resistance training program on physical function and muscle strength in community-dwelling elderly women. This study was part of the Healthy Aging and Happy Aging II project and was published in Geriatrics & Gerontology International in 2017, volume 17, issue 5, pages 825–833. 21. Wolf SL, Barnhart HX, Kutner NG, McNeely E, Coogler C, and Xu T investigated the effects of Tai Chi and computerized balance training on reducing frailty and falls in older adults. This study, recognized as one of the best papers of the 1990s, was published in Journal of the American Geriatrics Society in 2003, volume 51, issue 12, pages 1794–1803. 22. Goodpaster BH, Chomentowski P, Ward BK, Rossi A, Glynn NW, Delmonico MJ, et al. examined the effects of physical activity on strength and skeletal muscle fat infiltration in older adults. This randomized controlled trial was published in Journal of Applied Physiology in 2008, volume 105, issue 5, pages 1498–1503. 23. Kemmler W and von Stengel S explored the relationship between exercise frequency, health risk factors, and diseases in the elderly. Their findings were published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2013, volume 94, issue 11, pages 2046–2053.
